report.source_text: Due to multifocal cutaneous disease, there was high clinical suspicion of metastatic disease. Our patient was referred to medical and surgical oncology for further evaluation, and computed tomography (CT) scans of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis were performed. Innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules, a 1.8-cm hypoattenuated hepatic lesion, and prominent bilateral axillary lymph nodes were noted, all consistent with metastatic disease.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old woman presented with painful, progressively enlarging left posterior auricular and left preauricular papules. Biopsy of the lesions revealed cellular dermal proliferations of epithelioid cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm arranged in cords within a myxohyaline stroma, and subtle vacuoles containing red blood cells. Histological and immunohistochemical findings were consistent with the diagnosis of EHE. Subsequent CT scans for metastatic workup showed innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules, a hepatic lesion, and prominent bilateral axillary lymph nodes, consistent with metastatic disease. The patient elected a watchful waiting approach with serial CT scans every 3 months.
